title: Felwood
body: Felwood was once the northern reach of Ashenvale, a serene forest tended by the night elves beneath Mount Hyjal. In the Third War the Burning Legion made it a weapon. To weaken the kaldorei before the demons marched on Hyjal, the dreadlord Tichondrius used the Skull of Gul'dan to poison the land, and nothing was spared: the trees blackened, the beasts went mad, ancients were twisted and the waters turned foul. Illidan Stormrage later took the skull and destroyed Tichondrius, yet the taint remained, and so did the demons. The Shadow Council plots with the Legion from Jaedenar, Jadefire satyrs defile the old elven ruins, and infernals still stalk the craters where they fell. The Deadwood furbolgs have been driven mad, while in the north the Timbermaw alone of their race stayed pure. From the Emerald Sanctuary, druids of the Emerald Circle labor to heal what they can. The Horde keeps Bloodvenom Post on the western cliffs, and the night elves hold Talonbranch Glade in the north.

title: Morlos'Aran
body: At the southern edge of Felwood, near the Ashenvale border, stand the ruins of Morlos'Aran. Before the Sundering it was a great night elf settlement, kin to Ameth'Aran in Darkshore and Ordil'Aran in Ashenvale, and its broken stones now serve only to recall a golden age lost long ago. The corruption has not spared it. Felpaw wolves, Angerclaw bears and Ironbeak owls roam among the ruins, and the great wolf Death Howl hunts these southern woods. Here the night elf druid Arathandris Silversky of the Emerald Circle keeps her post, seeking anyone willing to help her reclaim Felwood.

title: Emerald Sanctuary
body: Hidden among the trees of southern Felwood, the Emerald Sanctuary is the camp of the Emerald Circle, a largely independent branch of the Cenarion Circle sworn to undo the corruption of this land. Its druids are friendly to all who come in peace. The tauren Greta Mosshoof directs the war on the Shadow Council, Eridan Bluewind strikes at the Jadefire satyrs, and Taronn Redfeather hunts in vain for a single pure source of water in the forest. Jessir Moonbow, come from Darnassus with her wolf Della, waits here for friends long overdue from Jaedenar. Nearby on the road stands Grazle, a Timbermaw furbolg seeking allies for his tribe.

title: Deadwood Village
body: Southwest of the Emerald Sanctuary, toward the Ashenvale border, lies Deadwood Village, the chief camp of the Deadwood furbolgs. Like most of their race they fell to the fel, which poisons their minds and turns them against all others. Deadwood warriors, pathfinders and gardeners fill its huts, and the Timbermaw ask their allies to drive this camp back first. The village answers to Overlord Ror, a great befouled furbolg, and the savage Ragepaw prowls nearby. Ror has claimed at least one hero: an orc warrior who roamed Felwood fighting the Shadow Council went after him at a druid's request, and neither was ever seen again.

title: Ruins of Constellas
body: Northwest of the Emerald Sanctuary stand the Ruins of Constellas, once one of the many night elf settlements near Mount Hyjal. Its moonwell, long a symbol of renewal for the kaldorei, has been fouled with fel energy, and the Jadefire satyrs who hold the ruins use its waters to bring forth more of their kind. Their leader here is the cruel Xavathras, who tends the corrupted well on behalf of Xavaric and spreads the sickness to every creature he can. Felsworn, shadowstalkers and rogues haunt the broken walls, cursed oozes seep among the stones, and the Forsaken of Bloodvenom Post have taken an interest in the well's water.

title: Jadefire Glen
body: In the south of Felwood, west of the Emerald Sanctuary, a wooded hollow called Jadefire Glen is one of the homes of the Jadefire satyrs, the tribe that has made the corruption of Felwood its feast. Satyrs and felsworn crowd the glade, and among them, seldom seen, walks Alshirr Banebreath. Even here a corrupted whipper root clings to life, waiting for a druid's salve to make it whole.

title: Bloodvenom Post
body: Bloodvenom Post is the Horde's only foothold in Felwood, a small camp on the high cliffs above Darkshore, close by the poisoned Bloodvenom River. Braves stand guard, a wind rider master links it to the rest of Kalimdor, and merchants trade goods and weapons. Those who linger have their own purposes. The Forsaken Winna Hazzard experiments with corrupted moonwell water, Trull Failbane looks beyond Timbermaw to Winterspring and the night elf secrets its wildkin are said to guard, and the orc widow Dreka'Sur waits for vengeance on the furbolg who took her husband.

title: Bloodvenom Falls
body: Through the heart of Felwood runs the Bloodvenom River, its water thick with the forest's poison, and at Bloodvenom Falls it spills into fouled pools where tainted oozes breed. The largest of them, a hulking mass called the Ongar, lurks below the falls. The riverbanks belong to the Shadow Council: its warlocks, darkweavers and enforcers walk them openly, and the tunnels of their fortress run beneath. The taint does not stay in Felwood. In Darkshore, Thundris Windweaver of Auberdine traces the fouling of the Cliffspring River east to this forest.

title: Jaedenar
body: West of the road in central Felwood lies Jaedenar, raised on ancient night elf ruins and druidic barrow dens and now named in worship of Kil'jaeden. It is the seat of the Shadow Council on Azeroth, the cult that claims credit for much of the suffering of the orcish people, and here it plots with the Burning Legion. Cultists, adepts and guardians patrol the ruins with their hounds, warlocks and darkweavers practice their arts, and legionnaires stand among them. At its center a moonwell still holds water, corrupt like all else here. Below lies Shadow Hold, the cult's fortress, warded by spells bound to burning braziers.

title: Shadow Hold
body: Beneath Jaedenar lies Shadow Hold, the Shadow Council's chief fortress, and a single path winds down through it with no other way in. Four braziers of protection, called Pain, Malice, Hatred and Suffering, keep its depths hidden from scrying eyes. The cult keeps prisoners caged and torturers at hand. The warlock Ulathek has his own quarters here and boasts that he holds counsel with dreadlords, and in his chamber the dreadlord Lord Banehollow keeps court with his attendant Ur'dan. In the deepest halls Shadow Lord Fel'dan, the mortal who leads the cult below, makes pacts with the Legion, attended by the succubi Moora and Salia.

title: Shrine of the Deceiver
body: Among the ruins of Jaedenar, one of the old druidic barrow dens has been given over to the Shadow Council and renamed the Shrine of the Deceiver, after Kil'jaeden, the lord of the Burning Legion whom the cult reveres. Where druids once slept, cultists, adepts and guardians keep its chambers with their hounds, and it is a dangerous place for the unprepared. The Emerald Circle sends would-be allies into these corrupted dens to thin the cult's ranks before trusting them with greater tasks.

title: Shatter Scar Vale
body: North of Bloodvenom Falls, east of the road, the land is pocked with craters where infernals were hurled down during the last great war. The craters still smolder and still hold the corrupt, fetid water that gathered in them years ago, and entropic beasts and horrors roam among them. The infernals themselves remain, brainless but destructive, and the mightiest of them is Immolatus. The vale has an unlikely resident too: the gnome warlock Niby the Almighty, who has made camp here with his imp near the burned-out remains of an infernal named Kroshius.

title: Jadefire Run
body: In the north of Felwood the Jadefire satyrs keep their second great encampment at Jadefire Run. Its master is the cruel Xavaric, to whom Xavathras sends the spoils of the corrupted moonwell at Constellas. Hellcallers and tricksters crowd the camp, feeding on the corruption of the forest's creatures. Xavaric carries a simple wooden flute that is far from simple: it was carved from an ancient protector, and the tortured spirit of that ancient remains bound within it.

title: Irontree Woods
body: Irontree Woods spreads across northern Felwood, once a peaceful glade and now as corrupted as the rest of the forest. Crazed treants, the irontree stompers and wanderers, roam alongside warpwood elementals, toxic horrors and maddened grizzlies and owls. Many corrupted treants once dwelt in the ruins at the southern edge of the woods, and their spirits may linger there still. Older presences remain as well. Vartrus, Stoma and Hastat, ancients who protected this forest and whose bodies were destroyed when the Legion marched upon Hyjal, still keep watch in spirit, offering their secrets only to those who prove worthy.

title: Irontree Cavern
body: A cavern beneath the Irontree Woods shelters warpwood elementals, moss flayers and shredders that the druids of the Emerald Circle believe are now beyond any hope of cleansing. Their sap, which the druids call blood amber, is studied by Arathandris Silversky and Maybess Riverbreeze in the hope of saving other life in Felwood, and killing these lost creatures is how both druids judge whether a stranger truly serves the Cenarion Circle. Deep in the cave lurks Dessecus, a powerful elemental.

title: Talonbranch Glade
body: Talonbranch Glade is a small night elf post in northern Felwood, south of Timbermaw Hold, built around a moonwell. It is the Alliance's only refuge in the corrupted forest. A hippogryph master links it to the other roosts of Kalimdor, and merchants offer weapons and supplies. Teachers keep the old disciplines alive here: Kaerbrus instructs hunters, Nalesette Wildbringer trains their pets, and the night elf druid Golhine the Hooded counsels that peace can be found anywhere, even within cold stone walls, by looking inward for balance. Golhine warns young druids that one day the Emerald Dream will call them to sleep for years and walk among the purest of forms.

title: Felpaw Village
body: In the far north of Felwood, just southwest of the gates of Timbermaw Hold, lies Felpaw Village, a camp of the Deadwood furbolgs. Den watchers, avengers and shamans guard it under Chieftain Bloodmaw, and corruption hangs heavy over its huts. Nafien, the Timbermaw guard at the nearby gate, grieves that his tribe must fight its own kin here. In the camp a cauldron bubbles with a rotting, repulsive sludge, and runners of the Winterfall tribe come down from Winterspring to carry shipments back to their village. The ritual totems its furbolgs carry give off a palpable despair.

title: Timbermaw Hold
body: Timbermaw Hold is the home of the Timbermaw furbolgs, cut into the mountains of northern Felwood, and its tunnels are the road from Felwood to Moonglade and Winterspring. While the forest outside rotted, the Timbermaw weathered the storm here, the only furbolg tribe to escape the corruption. They pay for it with suspicion. So many outsiders kill furbolgs on sight that the tribe trusts almost no one, and strangers who have not proven themselves are attacked within the hold. Nafien guards the Felwood gate and Salfa the Winterspring one. Inside, the gruff trader Gorn One Eye, Kernda, who studies the totems of the corrupted tribes, and Meilosh, who holds mooncloth sacred, deal with the few they trust.

title: Greta Mosshoof
body: Greta Mosshoof is a tauren druid of the Emerald Circle at the Emerald Sanctuary who leads the Circle's fight against the Shadow Council. She welcomes all who would protect this once mighty forest, but warns them not to be swayed by the power that soaks the land, for it will corrupt them as it corrupted Felwood. Her trust is earned in battle against the cult, and she explains why plainly: it weakens the foe, and it builds respect between allies. She prefers knowledge to haste, spying on Shadow Hold by scrying before any attack. She counts the shaman Islen Waterseer an old friend, and her prayers go to the Earthmother.

title: Eridan Bluewind
body: Eridan Bluewind is a night elf druid of the Emerald Circle who works from the Emerald Sanctuary. She notes the bitter truth that Felwood is named for the very thing that corrupted it, yet she still believes the corruption can one day be erased. Her chief enemies are the Jadefire satyrs, who spread their disease to every creature they touch, and she senses something larger than the satyrs at work in the forest. She can feel the suffering of ancients bound by fel magic, and with water blessed in the Temple of the Moon she has broken such a bond. Seekers of Un'Goro Crater's mysteries find their way to her as well.

title: Lord Banehollow
body: Lord Banehollow is a dreadlord and the master of Jaedenar, the seat of the Shadow Council on Azeroth. From his chamber in Shadow Hold he receives few visitors, and only those cloaked in the cult's own brand of evil, for though his patience spans millennia he grants a mortal no more than an instant. He has a rival in Lord Hel'nurath, whose domain is Xoroth, the world of the famed dreadsteeds. Banehollow's servant Ulathek grovels before him while secretly spying for that rival, and Banehollow knows it, and longs to feast on the traitor's heart. His attendant Ur'dan keeps a store of Xorothian stardust, which Banehollow parts with only for a price.

title: Niby the Almighty
body: Niby the Almighty is a gnome warlock camped in Shatter Scar Vale with his imp Impsy, and he demands that visitors bow before his power. Stormwind threw him out, and he has sworn revenge by calling down an infernal destroyer of his own. To a fellow warlock who brings him the burning core of the fallen infernal Kroshius, he will teach the secret of summoning such a servant. His own grand conjurations go less well: the mighty destroyer he calls from the sky turns out to be a chicken, though Niby promises Stormwind death by chicken all the same. Impsy rolls on the floor laughing and tells his master, often, that he is an idiot.

title: Arko'narin
body: Arko'narin is a night elf who came to Jaedenar with her longtime friend Trey Lightforge, a human Knight of the Silver Hand, to learn what the Shadow Council was planning. The cult caught them unprepared, took their equipment and locked her in a cage in Shadow Hold, while Trey was dragged deeper below. Cold and hungry, she could hear his screams rising from the depths, sounds she called inhuman. Even fearing he was already dead, she swore that the cultists would pay. Freed at last, she would not leave without his sword Lightforge, and she carried it to Darnassus to warn her superiors, too urgent even to stop for healing.

title: Arei
body: Arei is the spirit of one of Felwood's ancient protectors, bound to the land's suffering even after death. Arei remembers a peaceful and serene forest before the Legion came with its infernals, destruction and chaos, and the Skull of Gul'dan, which spared nothing. Trapped by the corruption, the spirit cannot rest, and asks only to be led out of the cursed forest toward Ashenvale. The way is hard: maddened creatures attack, and Arei grieves at having to fight its own kind. As Ashenvale draws near, its true strength returns and the forest's grip falls away. At peace at last, Arei sends its guide to the druid Kayneth Stillwind in Forest Song.

title: Grazle
body: Grazle is a Timbermaw furbolg who stands on the road near the Emerald Sanctuary, far from his tribe's hold, seeking friends among outsiders. He calls the Timbermaw the last of the furbolg race to remain uncorrupted, and it pains him that few believe such a thing possible. Most strangers kill furbolgs on sight, and in anger his brethren now attack anyone who comes near. Grazle still hopes that peace can be made with those who show by their deeds that they come as allies. To any who fight the corrupted Deadwood, he is a patient friend, and he makes sure their deeds are known among his kind.

title: Gorn One Eye
body: Gorn One Eye keeps a trader's stall deep in Timbermaw Hold and trusts very few outsiders, waving off newcomers who have won over only a handful of his kin. Through the help of trusted friends, the Timbermaw found a way to draw out the root of the Winterfall tribe's madness: the demon Xandivious, which dominates them and can be lured out at the mouth of High Chief Winterfall's cave. Once it falls and its essence is brought to Gorn, he hails its slayer as a hero of the furbolgs, for the Winterfall at last have a chance to survive. Gorn then sends an offering of peace to the Alliance and the Horde, whose leaders once tried to reach the Timbermaw.

title: Dreka'Sur
body: Dreka'Sur is an orc of Bloodvenom Post whose husband traveled Felwood for the honor of their clan, battling the Shadow Council and the forest's other abominations. He cheated death many times. His last letter told her that a druid had asked his help against a great befouled furbolg called Overlord Ror, and after that neither warrior nor druid was heard from again. Left a widow and unable to rest, Dreka'Sur wants Ror's clawed hand, caring nothing whether the beast is corrupt or merely savage. When the claw is brought to her, she takes comfort that her husband died in battle, as he would have wanted, and that his killer has paid.

title: Winna Hazzard
body: Winna Hazzard is a Forsaken at Bloodvenom Post who admits that some call her exceptionally cruel, though she insists she only wants the Horde to gain every advantage over the Alliance. Her newest interest is the corrupted moonwell at the Ruins of Constellas, once a symbol of renewal for the night elves and now a font that breeds satyrs. She poured a sample of its water over her own kitten, laughing as it doubled in size and grew stronger, then had the cat carried to the well itself to see what more the corruption could do. She is certain the Forsaken will find uses for that water against their enemies.

title: The Shadow Council in Jaedenar
body: Greta Mosshoof trusts no one against the Shadow Council until they have shed the cult's blood, so her allies first descend on Jaedenar to thin its hounds, guards, adepts and cultists. Her plan is patient. Braziers in Shadow Hold shield the cult from her scrying, and only purified water can douse them, so a canteen is filled at the corrupt moonwell in the heart of Jaedenar and carried to the Barrens shore south of Ratchet. There Greta's old friend, the shaman Islen Waterseer, wins the blessing of the water spirits and sends the water back with a warning that the Shadow Council is not to be trifled with. With the cleansed water the four braziers are put out, and before the warlocks can restore their wards Greta sees into the depths. The head of the serpent is Shadow Lord Fel'dan, the mortal making pacts with the Legion. The only way to him is the straight path down, and there he and his two succubi die. Without him, Greta hopes, the cult will turn on itself.

title: The Prisoner of Shadow Hold
body: Jessir Moonbow came from Darnassus to meet two friends at the Emerald Circle's camp, but they were days late. They had gone into Jaedenar to learn whether the Shadow Council was regaining its power. A strange key of red bone, carried by the cult's servants, leads to the answer: a cage within Shadow Hold, where the night elf Arko'narin is held. Freed, she will not flee without Lightforge, the sword of her friend Trey, a Knight of the Silver Hand. She recovers it with her gear and fights her way out past the cult's legionnaires, and then Trey himself appears, his tormented spirit turned against her. After the escape she hurries on to Darnassus, and Jessir, knowing how the loss will haunt her friend, asks one thing more: that Trey's torturer, the succubus Rakaiah, be slain and his remains carried back to the Sanctuary, so the paladin may be given proper respect.

title: The Jadefire Satyrs
body: Eridan Bluewind of the Emerald Circle has watched the Jadefire satyrs spread their disease through Felwood's creatures, and she means to defend a land that was once her people's. The first blow falls on the Ruins of Constellas, where the cruel Xavathras commands felsworn, shadowstalkers and rogues. His death is only a beginning. Eridan senses something larger behind the satyrs, and the truth soon follows: Xavathras had been cultivating the corrupted moonwell to pass its spoils to another, Xavaric, whose camp lies to the north. There hellcallers and tricksters feed upon the corruption of the forest's native beasts. Eridan sends her champion north to cut down Xavaric and his followers and end the suffering they cause, knowing that even then it will take long labor to repair the damage done.
sources: quests 4421, 4906 descriptions and reward texts

title: The Flute of Xavaric
body: Among Xavaric's belongings is a simple wooden flute whose carved spirals seem to move beneath the fingers, and whoever holds it feels a sudden dread. Eridan Bluewind can hardly bear to touch it. The flute, she explains, was carved from an ancient protector, one of the treants that long guarded the night elves, and through fel magic the satyrs have bound its spirit to suffer without release; the felbind other satyrs carry is surely part of the binding. Blessed water is drawn from the Temple of the Moon in Darnassus, and praying for Elune to guide her hands, Eridan breaks the link between flute and spirit. She believes the flute may now call the spirits of ancients if played in a sacred place, perhaps the ruins at the southern edge of Irontree Woods, where many corrupted treants once lived. Played there, it brings forth the spirit Arei, who begs to be led home.

title: Cleansing Felwood
body: Two druids of the Emerald Circle, the night elf Arathandris Silversky southeast of the Emerald Sanctuary and the tauren Maybess Riverbreeze to its west, know how to cleanse the forest's plants, but they guard that knowledge closely, for in the wrong hands it would spell disaster for Felwood. Trust is won in the Irontree Cavern, where warpwood elementals lost beyond saving are slain for the sap called blood amber. It may seem strange, Arathandris admits, but saving countless lives must justify the means. Then the druids share their craft. With a Cenarion beacon, one can see the corrupted soul shards that tainted beasts leave behind, and from such things the druids make Cenarion plant salve. Spread on the sick plants of Felwood, the salve works quickly: sickly songflowers, windblossoms, night dragons and slime-coated whipper roots shed their corruption and bloom healthy again.

title: Timbermaw Ally
body: Grazle of the Timbermaw knows that outsiders kill furbolgs without asking whether they are friend or foe, so his tribe trusts very few. To earn a place among its allies one must drive back the corrupted Deadwood, starting with the warriors, pathfinders and gardeners of the village southwest of the Sanctuary. Grazle then sends the proven north along the road to Nafien, who guards the gate of Timbermaw Hold. Nafien welcomes them but warns that his kin answer strangers with open hostility. He asks that the Deadwood camp to his southwest be broken, though he begs to be spared the details: the Deadwood are not evil by nature, only poisoned by the fel, and it grieves him to fight his own brethren. Victory, he says, is a hollow word. Trust grows slowly, through Deadwood feathers and ritual totems carried to the hold, until the Timbermaw at last welcome their friend within. Beyond lies Winterspring, where the Winterfall tribe has fallen to the same corruption.
